title.narrative: Gweru Urban Resilience, Inclusion and Socio-Economic Empowerment (U-RISE)

description.narrative: CAFOD & Caritas Gweru's work on the U-RISE program is centred around Outcome 2; i.e. Strengthened Urban Policy & Regulatory Environment. Outcome 2 strengthens the policy, regulatory and institutional environment shaping urban economic activity in Bulawayo, Gweru and Kwekwe. The programme responds to major barriers faced by informal traders, women, youth and persons with disabilities, including weak governance, outdated by laws and fragmented coordination. Through Output 2.1, Simuka will support inclusive, evidence-based policy reform using a Political Economy Analysis and Actor Based Change approach. Residents’ associations, youth and women’s groups, vendor unions and faith leaders will engage local and national authorities in structured policy dialogue, backed by social audits, public consultations and policy briefs to promote transparency and better service delivery. Output 2.2 builds Local Authorities’ capacity to manage formal and informal economic spaces more effectively. Tailored institutional support will strengthen inclusive planning, regulatory practices and market management. A key intervention is the development of Safe Inclusive Markets, providing secure, accessible and climate sensitive trading spaces—offering immediate, visible improvements for vulnerable market users while promoting coherent urban economic governance. Output 2.3 integrates Community Led Disaster Risk Management into urban governance systems. By updating hazard maps, improving early warning systems and co creating city level disaster action plans, the programme will help authorities anticipate and respond to climate related shocks. Women, youth and persons with disabilities will contribute directly to resilience planning to ensure solutions reflect diverse lived realities. These systems will also support activation of the programme’s crisis modifier. Together, these efforts will catalyse more inclusive, accountable and climate resilient urban governance.
